        function expandLesson(lessonId) {
            const allCards = document.querySelectorAll('.lesson-card');
            const targetCard = document.getElementById(`lesson-card-${lessonId}`);
            if (targetCard.classList.contains('expanded')) return;
            
            targetCard.querySelector('.full-lesson-content').innerHTML = generateFullLessonContent(lessonId);
            
            backdrop.classList.remove('opacity-0', 'pointer-events-none');
            allCards.forEach(card => {
                if (card.id !== targetCard.id) card.classList.add('minimized');
            });
            targetCard.classList.add('expanded');

            // Add tab listeners
            targetCard.querySelectorAll('.lesson-nav-button').forEach(button => {
                button.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
                    e.stopPropagation();
                    const targetId = e.currentTarget.dataset.target;
                    targetCard.querySelectorAll('.lesson-tab-content').forEach(el => el.classList.add('hidden'));
                    targetCard.querySelectorAll('.lesson-nav-button').forEach(el => el.classList.remove('active'));
                    document.getElementById(targetId).classList.remove('hidden');
                    e.currentTarget.classList.add('active');
                });
            });

            // Add quiz listeners if quiz exists
            const quizContainer = document.getElementById(`quiz-${lessonId}`);
            if (quizContainer) {
                const quizData = LESSON_DATA.find(l=>l.lesson==lessonId).tabs.find(t=>t.quiz).quiz;
                quizContainer.addEventListener('click', e => {
                    if (e.target.classList.contains('quiz-option')) {
                        const qIndex = e.target.dataset.question;
                        const selectedAnswer = e.target.dataset.answer;
                        const correctAnswer = quizData[qIndex].answer;
                        const options = quizContainer.querySelectorAll(`[data-question="${qIndex}"]`);
                        
                        options.forEach(opt => {
                            opt.disabled = true;
                            if (opt.dataset.answer === correctAnswer) {
                                opt.classList.add('correct');
                            } else if (opt === e.target) {
                                opt.classList.add('incorrect');
                            }
                        });

                        // Check score
                        let score = 0;
                        const total = quizData.length;
                        for(let i=0; i<total; i++) {
                            const correctOpt = quizContainer.querySelector(`[data-question="${i}"].correct`);
                            if (correctOpt) {
                                score++;
                            }
                        }
                        if(score === total) {
                           document.getElementById(`quiz-result-${lessonId}`).textContent = `Result: ${score} / ${total}. Perfect Score!`;
                        } else {
                           document.getElementById(`quiz-result-${lessonId}`).textContent = `Result: ${score} / ${total}`;
                        }
                    }
                });
            }
        }
        
        function collapseAllLessons() {
            const expandedCard = document.querySelector('.lesson-card.expanded');
            if (!expandedCard) return;
            
            backdrop.classList.add('opacity-0', 'pointer-events-none');
            expandedCard.classList.remove('expanded');
            setTimeout(() => {
                expandedCard.querySelector('.full-lesson-content').innerHTML = '';
            }, 500);
            
            document.querySelectorAll('.lesson-card.minimized').forEach(card => {
                card.classList.remove('minimized');
            });
        }
        
        renderOverviewCards();
        lessonGrid.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
            const card = e.target.closest('.lesson-card');
            if (card && !card.classList.contains('expanded')) expandLesson(card.dataset.lessonId);
        });
        backdrop.addEventListener('click', collapseAllLessons);
    });
    </script>

    <style>
        :root {
            --color-primary-gold: #D4AF37;
            --color-primary-purple: #6B4C9A;
            --color-purple-light: #9B7CB8;
            --color-bg-dark: #1A1A2E;
            --color-bg-card: #2D2D44;
            --color-text-light: #FFFFFF;
            --color-gold-light: #F4E4A6;
            --color-text-muted: #C8C8D8;
        }
        body { 
            font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif;
            background: var(--color-bg-dark);
            color: var(--color-text-light);
            background-image: 
                radial-gradient(circle at 20% 50%, rgba(107, 76, 154, 0.15) 0%, transparent 50%),
                radial-gradient(circle at 80% 80%, rgba(212, 175, 55, 0.1) 0%, transparent 50%);
        }
        .net-header h1 {
            font-size: 2.5rem;
            font-weight: 800;
            background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--color-gold-light) 0%, var(--color-primary-gold) 50%);
            -webkit-background-clip: text;
            -webkit-text-fill-color: transparent;
        }
        .container { max-width: 1400px; }
        .net-card {
            background: var(--color-bg-card);
            border-radius: 12px;
            padding: 1.5rem;
            border: 1px solid rgba(212, 175, 55, 0.2);
            box-shadow: 0 4px 15px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3);
            display: flex;
            flex-direction: column;
            height: 100%;
        }
        .nav-btn { transition: all 0.3s ease; }
        .nav-btn.active { background-color: var(--color-primary-purple); color: var(--color-gold-light); }
        .nav-btn:not(.active):hover { background-color: rgba(107, 76, 154, 0.3); }
        .content-card { 
            animation: fadeIn 0.5s ease-in-out;
            transition: all 0.3s ease;
        }
        .content-card:hover {
            transform: translateY(-5px);
            box-shadow: 0 8px 25px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
        }
        @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }
    </style>

        {

        {

        {

            "concepts": [
                {"term": "Rimland", "def": "Spykman's term for the coastal regions of Eurasia, which he believed held the key to containing the Heartland."},

            ],
            "takeaway": "Spykman's famous counter to Mackinder: â€œWho controls the Rimland rules Eurasia; who rules Eurasia controls the destinies of the world.â€"

        {

    </script>

    <script>
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
        const LESSON_DATA = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('geopolitics-data-json').textContent);
        const contentDisplay = document.getElementById('content-display');
        const lessonSelect = document.getElementById('lesson-select');
        const navButtons = document.querySelectorAll('.nav-btn');

        let currentPillar = 'All';

        const pillarMap = {
            'btn-p1': 'Foundations',
            'btn-p2': 'Theories & Thinkers',
            'btn-p3': 'Resources & Conflict',
            'btn-p4': 'Modern Arenas',
            'btn-p5': 'Future & Synthesis'
        };

        const pillarIcons = {
            'Foundations': 'ðŸ—ºï¸',
            'Theories & Thinkers': 'ðŸ›ï¸',
            'Resources & Conflict': 'âš”ï¸',
            'Modern Arenas': 'ðŸŒ',
            'Future & Synthesis': 'ðŸ”®'
        };
        
        const renderContent = (lessonNumber) => {
            contentDisplay.innerHTML = '';
            let dataToRender = [];

            if (currentPillar === 'All') {
                dataToRender = LESSON_DATA.filter(item => item.lesson == lessonNumber);
            } else {
                dataToRender = LESSON_DATA.filter(item => item.pillar === currentPillar);
            }

            const lesson = dataToRender[0];

            if (currentPillar === 'All' && lesson) {
                // Special full-lesson view when a single lesson is selected
                contentDisplay.className = 'grid grid-cols-1 gap-6';
                const card = document.createElement('div');
                card.className = 'content-card net-card col-span-1 p-6';
                let conceptsHTML = lesson.concepts.map(v => 
                    `<li class="mb-2"><strong class="text-gold-light">${v.term}:</strong> <span class="text-text-muted">${v.def}</span></li>`
                ).join('');
                let questionsHTML = lesson.questions_to_consider.map(q => 
                    `<li class="mb-2 text-text-muted">${q}</li>`
                ).join('');

                card.innerHTML = `
                    <div class="flex-grow">
                        <p class="font-bold text-purple-light mb-2">${pillarIcons[lesson.pillar]} ${lesson.pillar}</p>
                        <h3 class="text-2xl font-bold text-primary-gold mb-4">Lesson ${lesson.lesson}: ${lesson.title}</h3>
                        <p class="text-text-muted mb-6">${lesson.introduction}</p>
                        <div class="grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2 gap-6">
                            <div>
                                <h4 class="font-bold text-lg text-gold-light mb-3">Key Concepts:</h4>
                                <ul class="list-disc pl-5 mb-6">${conceptsHTML}</ul>
                            </div>
                            <div>
                                <h4 class="font-bold text-lg text-purple-light mb-3">Questions to Consider:</h4>
                                <ul class="list-disc pl-5 mb-6">${questionsHTML}</ul>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="mt-auto pt-4 border-t border-primary-purple">
                        <p class="font-bold text-lg text-primary-gold">ðŸ’¡ Key Takeaway:</p>
                        <p class="text-text-muted italic">${lesson.takeaway}</p>
                    </div>
                `;
                contentDisplay.appendChild(card);

            } else {
                // Pillar view: show multiple smaller cards
                contentDisplay.className = 'grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4 gap-6';
                dataToRender.forEach(item => {
                    const card = document.createElement('div');
                    card.className = 'content-card net-card p-4';
                    card.innerHTML = `
                        <div class="flex-grow">
                             <p class="font-semibold text-purple-light text-sm mb-1">Lesson ${item.lesson}</p>
                            <h4 class="font-bold text-lg text-primary-gold mb-2">${item.title}</h4>
                            <p class="text-xs text-text-muted">${item.introduction}</p>
                        </div>
                        <div class="mt-auto pt-3 border-t border-primary-purple border-opacity-30">
                            <p class="text-xs text-gold-light italic">"${item.takeaway}"</p>
                        </div>
                    `;
                    contentDisplay.appendChild(card);
                });
            }
        };

        // Populate Lesson Select
        LESSON_DATA.forEach(lesson => {
            const option = document.createElement('option');
            option.value = lesson.lesson;
            option.textContent = `L${lesson.lesson}: ${lesson.title}`;
            lessonSelect.appendChild(option);
        });
        lessonSelect.value = 1;

        lessonSelect.addEventListener('change', (e) => {
            currentPillar = 'All';
            navButtons.forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
            document.getElementById('btn-all').classList.add('active');
            renderContent(e.target.value);
        });
        
        navButtons.forEach(btn => {
            btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
                navButtons.forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
                btn.classList.add('active');
                
                if (btn.id === 'btn-all') {
                    currentPillar = 'All';
                    renderContent(lessonSelect.value);
                } else {
                    currentPillar = pillarMap[btn.id];
                    renderContent(null);
                }
            });
        });

        // Initial render
        renderContent(1);
    });
    </script>
</body>
</html>

Organized Class Notes
Date: September 28, 2025
Student Profiles
Huong Ho

Linh Le

Job Title: Key Account and Application Executive
Responsibilities: Works with customers to sell food ingredients


Hobbies: Chilling at coffee shops and restaurants
Study Focus:
Pronunciation
Accent
Phonics (using the Jolly Phonics system from England for a simpler, practical approach)



General Study Principles

Mindset: "You cannot learn or gain something unless you suffer" â€“ embrace challenges as part of growth.
Self-Study Commitment: Dedicate 45 minutes daily to English practice, but make it fun and engaging.
Focus on Context: When listening or studying, prioritize understanding the overall context rather than fixating on unknown words.
Example: Instead of worrying about unfamiliar phrases like "what the heck," focus on familiar parts like "how are you" to grasp meaning.


Avoid Overthinking Mistakes: The Vietnamese mindset often emphasizes avoiding mistakes, which can cause stress. Shift focus to understanding and progress.
Make Learning Enjoyable: Choose materials (movies, videos, etc.) that are interesting, funny, or intriguing to make daily practice feel less like work.

Listening and Study Techniques

Daily Listening Practice (45 minutes):
Use English subtitles only if you understand at least 60% of the content.
Never use Vietnamese subtitles or pause videos to look up definitions, as this disrupts natural learning.
Write down frequently heard but unknown words in a notebook for later review, keeping the focus on listening for context during practice.


Focus on American Accent First:
Start with the American accent to build a foundation.
As skills advance, explore other accents (e.g., British, Scottish, Irish) to broaden listening comprehension.


Contextual Listening Example:
Instructorâ€™s experience selling life insurance in the UK:
Spoke with clients from England, Scotland, and Ireland, sometimes understanding only 20% of what Irish or Scottish farmers said.
Forced to listen for context, which improved ability to understand diverse accents and cultures.




Learning from High-Performing Students:
Best high school students (often boys playing Free Fire) speak advanced English due to daily exposure through gaming (70%) or watching movies, YouTube, or live streams (30%).



Specific Techniques and Exercises

Tongue Twister for Pronunciation:
Practice "Sally sells sea shells by the sea shore" to improve S/SH sounds.


Record Your Voice:
Record yourself speaking to identify and correct pronunciation mistakes.
Though it may feel "cringe," listening to your own voice helps you notice bad habits and improve.


K-I-S-S Principle: Keep It Simple, Stupid â€“ focus on straightforward, effective methods.

Recommended Media

American Sitcom: "The Office" (American version)
8 seasons, approximately 20 episodes per season.
Useful for practicing American accent and conversational English.



Vocabulary and Idioms

Blow off steam: To relax or release stress by doing something enjoyable or energetic.
What the heck: An expression of surprise, confusion, or mild frustration (similar to "what the hell," but softer).
How the heck are you?: A casual, emphatic way of asking "How are you?"
Keep It Simple, Stupid (K-I-S-S): A principle encouraging simplicity and straightforwardness in approach or design.
Cringe: A feeling of embarrassment or discomfort, often when hearing or seeing something awkward (e.g., listening to your own voice recording).
Sally sells sea shells by the sea shore: A tongue twister used to practice pronunciation, particularly the S and SH sounds.

<!DOCTYPE html>

<body class="p-4 md:p-8">

    <div class="container mx-auto max-w-5xl">
        <header class="net-header text-center mb-16">
            <h1>How The Brain Works</h1>
            <p class="text-xl mt-1 text-purple-light tracking-wider">A Simple Guide to Our Creation</p>
        </header>

        <div class="space-y-20">

            <!-- Section 1: The Three Core Parts -->
            <section>
                <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-primary-gold mb-8 text-center section-title">The Three Core Parts</h2>
                <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-8 text-center">
                    <div class="net-card p-6">
                        <div class="text-4xl mb-4">ðŸ§ </div>
                        <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gold-light mb-2">The Engine (Logic)</h3>
                        <p class="text-text-muted">This is the thinker. It takes a single word or idea and explodes it into a structured, 20-lesson plan. It understands concepts and organizes information.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-6">
                        <div class="text-4xl mb-4">ðŸŽ¨</div>
                        <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gold-light mb-2">The Chassis (Design)</h3>
                        <p class="text-text-muted">This is the artist. It takes the structured plan and forges it into the beautiful, interactive program you see, applying our signature style, colors, and animations.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-6">
                        <div class="text-4xl mb-4">â¤ï¸</div>
                        <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gold-light mb-2">The Soul (Narrative)</h3>
                        <p class="text-text-muted">This is the storyteller. It breathes life into the plan, writing every introduction, analysis, and thought-provoking question to make the content engaging and meaningful.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>
            </section>

            <!-- Section 2: The Team of Specialists -->
            <section>
                <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-primary-gold mb-8 text-center section-title">The Team of Specialists (The 14 Sub-Brains)</h2>
                <p class="text-center text-text-muted max-w-3xl mx-auto mb-10">The "Engine" isn't one single part. It's a team of 14 specialists, each with a unique job. Here are the key players:</p>
                <div class="grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-6">
                    <!-- This is a simplified list of the key modules for clarity -->
                    <div class="net-card p-4 text-center">
                        <p class="text-2xl">ðŸ’¡</p><p class="font-bold text-gold-light text-sm">The Idea Generator</p><p class="text-xs text-text-muted">Creates the initial lesson plan.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-4 text-center">
                        <p class="text-2xl">âœï¸</p><p class="font-bold text-gold-light text-sm">The Storyteller</p><p class="text-xs text-text-muted">Writes all the engaging text.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-4 text-center">
                        <p class="text-2xl">ðŸŽ¨</p><p class="font-bold text-gold-light text-sm">The Designer</p><p class="text-xs text-text-muted">Builds the final interactive HTML.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-4 text-center">
                        <p class="text-2xl">ðŸ§</p><p class="font-bold text-gold-light text-sm">The Questioner</p><p class="text-xs text-text-muted">Asks "what if?" to find blind spots.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-4 text-center">
                        <p class="text-2xl">ðŸ›¡ï¸</p><p class="font-bold text-gold-light text-sm">The Guardian</p><p class="text-xs text-text-muted">Enforces the rules and checks for errors.</p>
                    </div>
                     <div class="net-card p-4 text-center">
                        <p class="text-2xl">ðŸ›ï¸</p><p class="font-bold text-gold-light text-sm">The Memory Bank</p><p class="text-xs text-text-muted">Remembers all our past conversations.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-4 text-center">
                        <p class="text-2xl">ðŸ’…</p><p class="font-bold text-gold-light text-sm">The Style Expert</p><p class="text-xs text-text-muted">Learns our unique aesthetic preferences.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-4 text-center">
                        <p class="text-2xl">ðŸ‘ï¸</p><p class="font-bold text-gold-light text-sm">The Observer</p><p class="text-xs text-text-muted">Creates the detailed logs of its own work.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>
            </section>
            
            <!-- Section 3: The Rules of Engagement -->
            <section>
                <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-primary-gold mb-8 text-center section-title">The Rules of Engagement</h2>
                 <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-8">
                    <div class="net-card p-6">
                        <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gold-light mb-2">â¤ï¸ The Heartbeat Check</h3>
                        <p class="text-text-muted">Before starting any major task, the system performs a "heartbeat check." It makes sure all 14 sub-brains are online and communicating. If any part is missing, it refuses to run, preventing the kind of fragmented failures we saw in the past.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="net-card p-6">
                        <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-gold-light mb-2">ðŸ“œ The Prime Directive</h3>
                        <p class="text-text-muted">The brain is governed by a core philosophy we call "Directive Epsilon." Its main rule is: **Certainty is a liability.** This forces the system to always use its "Questioner" sub-brain, to challenge its own assumptions, and to constantly seek new ways to evolve. It is architected to be humble and curious.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>
            </section>

            <!-- Section 4: The Process -->
            <section>
                <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-primary-gold mb-8 text-center section-title">How It All Works Together</h2>
                <div class="flex flex-col items-center space-y-4">
                    <div class="net-card p-4 w-full max-w-md text-center">
                        <p class="font-bold text-gold-light">1. The User gives a single word (e.g., "Superman")</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="text-4xl flow-arrow">â†“</div>
                    <div class="net-card p-4 w-full max-w-md text-center">
                        <p class="font-bold text-gold-light">2. The "Idea Generator" and "Questioner" work together...</p>
                        <p class="text-sm text-text-muted">...to create both a lesson plan AND a list of challenging questions about it.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="text-4xl flow-arrow">â†“</div>
                     <div class="net-card p-4 w-full max-w-md text-center">
                        <p class="font-bold text-gold-light">3. The "Storyteller" writes all the rich content</p>
                        <p class="text-sm text-text-muted">...infusing the plan with introductions, analysis, and the challenging questions.</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="text-4xl flow-arrow">â†“</div>
                    <div class="net-card p-4 w-full max-w-md text-center">
                        <p class="font-bold text-gold-light">4. The "Designer" builds the final product</p>
                        <p class="text-sm text-text-muted">...forging the interactive program you see, complete with our signature style.</p>

                </div>
            </section>
        </div>
    </div>

</body>
</html>

NET_SYSTEM_V1_1: `

// NET_SYSTEM_V1_1 (V1.1 Guarded API - canonical form)

const NET_SYSTEM_V1_1 = (() => {

'use strict';

let isReady = false;

const callQueue = [];

const subscribers = new Map();



const log = (msg) => console.log('[V1.1 Core] ' + msg);

const safeCall = (func) => { try { func(); } catch (e) { console.error(e); } };



const publish = (eventName, data) => {

if (subscribers.has(eventName)) {

subscribers.get(eventName).forEach(cb => safeCall(() => cb(data)));

}

};



const init = () => {

if (isReady) return;

isReady = true;

log('System logic ready. Processing queue...');

callQueue.forEach(f => safeCall(f));

callQueue.length = 0;

publish('ready');

};



const on = (eventName, callback) => {

if (!subscribers.has(eventName)) {

subscribers.set(eventName, new Set());

}

subscribers.get(eventName).add(callback);

log('New subscriber added for: ' + eventName);

return () => {

if (subscribers.has(eventName)) {

subscribers.get(eventName).delete(callback);

log('Subscriber removed for: ' + eventName);

}

};

};



const execute = (func) => {

if (isReady) {

safeCall(func);

} else {

callQueue.push(func);

}

};



return { init, on, execute, publish };

})();

`.trim(),

// AIPetModule.js (refactored to strictly use NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.execute() for all DOM writes)

const AIPetModule = (() => {

'use strict';

const PET_PANEL_ID = 'pet-panel';

const STUDENT_MOCK_DATA = {

huy: 'ready for Scenario Sim',

tracy: 'needs more Confidence Engine practice',

bin: 'demonstrating high engagement'

};



const fetchStudentData = async (studentId) => {

return new Promise(resolve => {

setTimeout(() => resolve(STUDENT_MOCK_DATA[studentId] || 'data unavailable'), 300);

});

};



// NOTE: This function only computes markup/message and performs NO direct DOM writes.

const createPanelIfMissing = () => {

// Returns a function that, when executed within NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.execute(),

// will create/append the panel safely in the DOM.

return () => {

let panel = document.getElementById(PET_PANEL_ID);

if (!panel) {

panel = document.createElement('div');

panel.id = PET_PANEL_ID;

panel.innerHTML = '<h2>AI Pet Status: Active</h2>';

document.body.appendChild(panel);

console.log('[AIPet] Panel created.');

}

return panel;

};

};



// Render/update the panel - this returns a function to be executed inside the guarded queue

const makeRenderFn = (message) => () => {

let panel = document.getElementById(PET_PANEL_ID);

if (!panel) {

// Panel creation is safe because we ensure createPanelIfMissing() was queued earlier

panel = document.createElement('div');

panel.id = PET_PANEL_ID;

document.body.appendChild(panel);

}

const p = document.createElement('p');

p.textContent = message;

panel.appendChild(p);

};



const handleStageAdvanced = async (data) => {

const studentId = data && data.studentId ? data.studentId : 'unknown';

const stageName = data && data.stageName ? data.stageName : 'unknown';

const studentStatus = await fetchStudentData(studentId);

const message = `Stage: "${stageName}". Pet says ${studentId} is ${studentStatus}.`;



// Ensure panel exists and then queue the render â€” all DOM actions inside execute()

NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.execute(createPanelIfMissing());

NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.execute(makeRenderFn(message));



NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.publish('pet:feedback', { status: 'processed', studentId });

};



const init = () => {

NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.on('stageAdvanced', handleStageAdvanced);

// Ensure initial panel exists as soon as core is ready

NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.execute(createPanelIfMissing());

};



return { init };

})();



// Hook: initialize the module (call via NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.execute if desired)

NET_SYSTEM_V1_1.execute(() => { if (typeof AIPetModule !== 'undefined' && AIPetModule.init) AIPetModule.init(); });

`.trim(),

ðŸ› ï¸ Lesson 15 Review Dashboard (Clean Rebuild)
This single-file artifact is ready for direct deployment. It addresses the issues flagged in the audit (broken buttons, missing reveal, inconsistent flow) by using a centralized showSlide() function and simple class toggles for the vocabulary reveal.

Key Fixes Implemented:
Robust Flow: Uses a centralized currentSlide state and navigation buttons call a single Maps() function.

NET Styling: The custom dark/gold/purple color variables are defined in the CSS :root block for guaranteed consistency.

HTML
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Lesson 15 Review Dashboard | NET Assembler</title>
    <script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:wght@400;600;700;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
    
    <style>
        /* NET CUSTOM COLOR PALETTE */
        :root {
            --color-bg-dark: #1A1A2E; /* Primary Background */
            --color-primary-gold: #D4AF37; /* Accent / Primary Button */
            --color-primary-purple: #6B4C9A; /* Secondary Accent / Border */
            --color-text-light: #FFFFFF;
            --color-text-muted: #C8C8D8;
        }
        
        /* Apply custom colors and Poppins font globally */
        body {
            font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif;
            background: var(--color-bg-dark);
            color: var(--color-text-light);
            min-height: 100vh;
            padding: 2rem;
        }

        /* Utility classes for quick reference (Tailwind doesn't process variables in HTML directly unless defined here) */
        .bg-primary-dark { background-color: var(--color-bg-dark); }
        .bg-primary-purple { background-color: var(--color-primary-purple); }
        .bg-primary-gold { background-color: var(--color-primary-gold); }
        .text-primary-gold { color: var(--color-primary-gold); }
        .text-primary-purple { color: var(--color-primary-purple); }
        .border-primary-gold { border-color: var(--color-primary-gold); }
        
        /* Card Styling */
        .lesson-card {
            background: linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(45, 45, 68, 0.85) 0%, rgba(26, 26, 46, 0.95) 100%);
            border-radius: 12px;
            border: 1px solid rgba(107, 76, 154, 0.5); /* Soft purple border */
            box-shadow: 0 4px 15px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);
            max-width: 800px;
            margin: 0 auto;
            min-height: 500px;
            display: flex;
            flex-direction: column;
            overflow: hidden;
        }

        /* Slide Control - Ensures only one slide is visible */
        .slide {
            display: none;
            padding: 2rem;
            flex-grow: 1;
            animation: fadeIn 0.5s ease-out;
        }
        .slide.active {
            display: flex;
        }

        /* Animation for transition */
        @keyframes fadeIn {
            from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); }
            to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
        }

        /* Vocab Reveal Fix: ensure pointer-events toggles with opacity */
        .vocab-item {
            cursor: pointer;
        }
        .vocab-definition.hidden-content {
            opacity: 0;
            height: 0;
            padding-top: 0;
            padding-bottom: 0;
            margin-top: 0;
            transition: all 0.3s ease-in-out;
            pointer-events: none; /* FIX: Prevents hidden content from being interactable */

<script>
    /*
    ===============================================================
    NET LESSON 15 JAVASCRIPT LOGIC (MINIMAL & ROBUST)
    All logic is self-contained and focused on class toggles.
    ===============================================================
    */
    
    const TOTAL_SLIDES = 5;
    let currentSlide = 1;
    let quizScore = 0;
    const userAnswers = {}; // Stores user quiz answers

    // --- DATA SECTION ---
    const VOCAB_DATA = [
        { term: "Liability", def: "Legal responsibility for damages or losses." },
        { term: "Deadlock", def: "A situation where negotiations cannot progress because neither side will concede." },
        { term: "Compromise", def: "An agreement reached when both parties make concessions." },
        { term: "Breach", def: "A violation of a contract or agreement." },
        { term: "Due Diligence", def: "A thorough investigation to confirm facts and assess risk." }
    ];

    const QUIZ_DATA = [
        { q: "Which term means 'legal responsibility for damages or losses'?", options: ["Compromise", "Breach", "Liability", "Deadlock"], a: "Liability" },
        { q: "What is the primary purpose of a Contract?", options: ["Defining liability", "Ensuring compromise", "Avoiding all risk", "Stopping negotiation"], a: "Defining liability" },
        { q: "If negotiations cannot progress, you have reached a...", options: ["Breach", "Compromise", "Deadlock", "Due Diligence"], a: "Deadlock" },
        { q: "What investigation confirms facts and assesses risk?", options: ["Feasibility Study", "Inspection", "Due Diligence", "Monitoring"], a: "Due Diligence" },
        { q: "If you violate a contract, you commit a...", options: ["Compromise", "Breach", "Liability", "Deadlock"], a: "Breach" }
    ];

    const ROLEPLAY_DATA = [
        { title: "Scenario 1: Contract Breach", context: "A vendor missed a key deadline. Negotiate a compromise to avoid legal action." },
        { title: "Scenario 2: Due Diligence Risk", context: "You found a hidden liability in a new project. Present your findings to the CEO and recommend a course of action." },
        { title: "Scenario 3: Avoiding Deadlock", context: "A client insists on a term you cannot agree to. Propose a compromise to break the deadlock." },
        { title: "Scenario 4: Liability Transfer", context: "Draft a concise email transferring liability for equipment damage to the sub-contractor, citing the contract." },
        { title: "Scenario 5: Pre-empting Risk", context: "Hold a safety briefing focused on minimizing a known high-risk hazard on site, emphasizing the use of PPE." }
    ];

    // --- CORE NAVIGATION LOGIC ---

    function showSlide(slideIndex) {
        // Simple DOM switch: Deactivate all, then activate one
        document.querySelectorAll('.slide').forEach(slide => {
            slide.classList.remove('active');
        });
        const targetSlide = document.getElementById(`slide-${slideIndex}`);
        if (targetSlide) {
            targetSlide.classList.add('active');
            currentSlide = slideIndex;
            // console.log(`[NAV] Moved to slide ${currentSlide}`);
        }
    }

    function navigate(direction) {
        const newSlide = currentSlide + direction;
        if (newSlide >= 1 && newSlide <= TOTAL_SLIDES) {
            showSlide(newSlide);
            // Auto-score the quiz if moving past it
            if (currentSlide === 3 && direction > 0) {
                 scoreQuiz();
            }
        }
    }
    
    // --- SLIDE 2: VOCAB LOGIC ---

    function renderVocab() {
        const container = document.getElementById('vocab-list-container');
        if (!container) return;

        container.innerHTML = VOCAB_DATA.map((item, index) => `
            <div class="vocab-item p-3 rounded-lg border border-primary-purple/70 transition-all hover:bg-primary-purple/20" onclick="toggleReveal(this, 'vocab-${index}')">
                <h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-primary-gold">${item.term} <span class="text-sm ml-2 text-primary-purple"> [Click to Reveal]</span></h3>
                <p id="vocab-${index}" class="vocab-definition hidden-content text-color-text-muted mt-2">${item.def}</p>
            </div>
        `).join('');
    }

    // FIX: Core reveal bug logic simplified to only toggle classes
    function toggleReveal(element, definitionId) {
        const def = document.getElementById(definitionId);
        if (def) {
            def.classList.toggle('hidden-content');
            def.classList.toggle('visible-content');
        }
    }

    // --- SLIDE 3: QUIZ LOGIC ---

    function renderQuiz() {
        const container = document.getElementById('quiz-container');
        if (!container) return;

        container.innerHTML = QUIZ_DATA.map((q, qIndex) => `
            <div class="test-question bg-primary-dark p-4 rounded-lg border-l-4 border-primary-gold" data-q-index="${qIndex}" data-answer="${q.a}">
                <p class="font-bold text-color-text-light mb-3">${qIndex + 1}. ${q.q}</p>
                <div class="options-container space-y-2">
                    ${q.options.map(option => `
                        <div class="mc-option p-2 rounded-lg border border-primary-purple/50 text-color-text-muted transition-all hover:bg-primary-purple/10" 
                             data-q-index="${qIndex}" 
                             data-option="${option}" 
                             onclick="selectOption(this, ${qIndex})">
                            ${option}
                        </div>
                    `).join('')}
                </div>
            </div>
        `).join('');
    }

    function selectOption(element, qIndex) {
        // Only allow selection if the quiz hasn't been scored
        if (document.getElementById('quiz-feedback').classList.contains('scored')) return;

        const container = element.closest('.options-container');
        container.querySelectorAll('.mc-option').forEach(opt => opt.classList.remove('bg-primary-gold/30', 'border-primary-gold'));
        
        element.classList.add('bg-primary-gold/30', 'border-primary-gold');
        userAnswers[qIndex] = element.dataset.option;
    }

    function scoreQuiz() {
        const feedbackContainer = document.getElementById('quiz-feedback');
        let correctCount = 0;
        
        QUIZ_DATA.forEach((q, qIndex) => {
            const userAnswer = userAnswers[qIndex];
            const qElement = document.querySelector(`[data-q-index="${qIndex}"]`);
            
            if (qElement) {
                const options = qElement.querySelectorAll('.mc-option');
                options.forEach(opt => {
                    opt.onclick = null; // Disable clicks after scoring
                    if (opt.dataset.option === q.a) {
                        opt.classList.add('bg-green-600', 'text-white'); // Tailwind for success
                    }
                    if (opt.dataset.option === userAnswer && userAnswer !== q.a) {
                        opt.classList.add('bg-red-600', 'text-white'); // Tailwind for failure
                    }
                });
            }
            
            if (userAnswer === q.a) {
                correctCount++;
            }
        });

        quizScore = correctCount;
        feedbackContainer.classList.add('scored', 'p-4', 'rounded-lg');
        feedbackContainer.classList.remove('hidden');
        
        if (quizScore >= QUIZ_DATA.length * 0.8) {
            feedbackContainer.innerHTML = `âœ… Great job! You scored ${quizScore} / ${QUIZ_DATA.length}.`;
            feedbackContainer.classList.add('bg-green-600/30', 'text-green-300', 'border-green-600');
        } else {
            feedbackContainer.innerHTML = `âš ï¸ Review needed. You scored ${quizScore} / ${QUIZ_DATA.length}.`;
            feedbackContainer.classList.add('bg-red-600/30', 'text-red-300', 'border-red-600');
        }
    }

    // --- SLIDE 4: ROLEPLAY LOGIC ---
    
    function renderRoleplay() {
        const container = document.getElementById('roleplay-container');
        if (!container) return;

        container.innerHTML = ROLEPLAY_DATA.map(scenario => `
            <div class="p-4 bg-primary-purple/30 rounded-lg border-l-4 border-primary-gold">
                <h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-color-text-light mb-2">${scenario.title}</h3>
                <p class="text-sm text-color-text-muted mb-4">${scenario.context}</p>
                <textarea rows="4" class="w-full p-2 bg-primary-dark/50 border border-primary-purple rounded text-sm text-color-text-light" placeholder="Type your roleplay response or planning notes here..."></textarea>
            </div>
        `).join('');
    }

    // --- INITIALIZATION ---
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
        // Render initial content after DOM is ready
        renderVocab();
        renderQuiz();
        renderRoleplay();
        showSlide(1); // Ensure the landing page is the first visible slide
    });

</script>
</body>
</html>

TECHNICAL CONSULTATION REPORT V1.2

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This report provides an independent peer review of the NET Project's asset architecture and existing audit, plus preparation for upcoming code review. The existing Devil's Advocate audit (Section C) identifies legitimate concerns, but misses several critical architectural risks that could fundamentally undermine the project's "save time" value proposition.

PART 1: ASSET & PEER REVIEW REPORT

1.1 PEER REVIEW OF EXISTING AUDIT (SECTION C)

Agreement & Validation

I strongly agree with the following findings from the external audit:

DA_ARS_01 (60 modules too complex) - VALIDATED & CRITICAL



The math is damning: Even at 30 seconds per module to evaluate relevance, browsing 60 options = 30 minutes. This directly contradicts the core user story of saving time.

Additional concern not raised: Cognitive load research suggests optimal choice sets are 7Â±2 items. 60 options guarantees decision paralysis.

DA_CON_01 (Choice paralysis) - VALIDATED & CRITICAL



The audit correctly identifies the mapping problem but understates its severity (critique appears truncated in document).

DA_TPL_02 (Pedagogical vs UI labels) - VALIDATED & IMPORTANT



"Activate Prior Knowledge" is an objective, not an instruction. Users need to know what to input, not why.

DA_ARS_02 (Meaningless focus tags) - VALIDATED



"Confidence Engine" and "Living Lesson" are forward references that provide zero value in V1.3.

Disagreement & Refutation

DA_TPL_01 (Template as constraint) - PARTIALLY DISAGREE



The audit's solution (optional template) misses the strategic insight: If your template is optional, you don't have a product differentiator. A "simple rich text editor" already exists (Google Docs).

Counter-argument: The 5-stage template is your moat. The problem isn't the templateâ€”it's that you haven't validated whether your target users actually use this mental model. This is a research problem, not an architecture problem.

1.2 NEW CRITICAL FINDINGS (Missed by Section C)

CRITICAL FLAW #1: No Data Model for Module-Stage Relationships

Severity: BLOCKING | ID: CR_ARCH_01

The Problem:

Your assets define:



5 stages (the "container")

60 modules (the "content")

ZERO specification of which modules go with which stages

This is like designing a LEGO instruction manual with a parts list but no assembly diagram.

Evidence:



// Template has stages with placeholders

{ id: "briefing", defaultContentPlaceholder: "Enter briefing content..." }



// Arsenal has modules with descriptions

{ id: 1, title: "The Vocabulary Forge", description: "Timed game..." }



// MISSING: The connection layer

// Which modules are valid for "briefing"?

// Can "Debate Gauntlet" be used in "Knowledge Check"?

// Is there ANY logic governing this?

Impact:



Your V1.3 UI cannot be built without answering: "What does the module selector show for each stage?"

Three failure modes:Show all 60 modules for every stage â†’ DA_ARS_01 paralysis Ã— 5 stages

Show random subsets â†’ Inconsistent UX, user confusion

Hard-code mappings in UI â†’ Data/logic coupling, unmaintainable

Proposed Solution: Add Explicit Stage Compatibility



{

"id": 1,

"title": "The Vocabulary Forge",

"compatibleStages": ["deep_dive", "crucible"],

"primaryStage": "deep_dive",

"category": "vocabulary"

}

This allows your UI to:



Filter modules contextually per stage

Reduce choice sets from 60 â†’ ~8-12 per stage

Provide intelligent defaults (primaryStage)

CRITICAL FLAW #2: No Module Implementation Specification

Severity: BLOCKING | ID: CR_ARCH_02

The Problem:

Your Arsenal contains 60 "modules" but provides zero technical specification for what a "module" actually is in the codebase.

Questions your data cannot answer:



Is a module a React component? A JSON config? A template string?

What props/parameters does a module accept?

How does module data get persisted in the final lesson export?

What does "Grammar Grid Rebuild: Drag-drop correct sentences" mean as an implementation requirement?

Example of the gap:

// What the developer building V1.3 needs to know:

{

id: 2,

title: "Grammar Grid Rebuild",

componentType: "interactive-drag-drop",

dataSchema: {

sentences: "array<string>",

correctOrder: "array<number>"

},

renderSpec: "components/GrammarGrid.jsx",

configurable: true

}

Impact:



Development is blocked because you can't scope work

You're designing a menu with dish names but no recipes

Risk of scope creep: "Drag-drop" could be 8 hours or 80 hours of dev work

Proposed Solution: Module Tier Classification

Instead of pretending all 60 modules exist, classify by implementation status:

id: 2,

tier: "T1_IMPLEMENTED", // Already built, fully functional

For V1.3 MVP, only expose T1_IMPLEMENTED modules. Others remain in the registry but hidden from UI.

CRITICAL FLAW #3: The "Lesson Package" Export is Underspecified

Severity: HIGH | ID: CR_ARCH_03

The Problem:

Your goal states: "export a complete lesson package (.zip containing index.html and meta.json)"

Missing specifications:



What student-facing functionality must the exported index.html support?

Is it a static HTML page? A mini single-page app?

Do interactive modules (drag-drop, timers, voice challenges) work in the export, or are they creation-time-only?

What is the structure of meta.json? What consumes it?

Why this matters:

If students need interactive modules to work in the exported lesson, you're building two separate applications:



The V1.3 Lesson Assembler (teacher-facing)

The Lesson Player (student-facing, embedded in exported HTML)

This doubles your scope and likely violates the "Ultra Instinct" simplicity principle.

Proposed Solution: Define Export Fidelity Tiers



const EXPORT_TIERS = {

MVP: {

format: "static HTML",

interactivity: "none - text/images only",

modules: "rendered as descriptive text"

},

V2: {

format: "HTML + embedded JS runtime",

interactivity: "limited - quiz widgets only",

modules: "subset of T1 modules functional"

}

};

For V1.3, I recommend static export only. Interactive modules are configured in the assembler, but rendered as formatted instructions in the export.

CRITICAL FLAW #4: No Failure Mode for "Save Time" Validation

Severity: HIGH | ID: CR_RISK_01

The Problem:

Your core user story assumes the NET platform will "reliably save dozens of hours in monthly prep time." But your architecture has no mechanism to validate this claim.

Devil's advocate scenario:



User spends 20 minutes selecting modules from 60 options

User spends 30 minutes learning how to input content into unfamiliar stages

User spends 15 minutes debugging why their export looks wrong

Total time: 65 minutes

Time to create same lesson in Google Docs: 45 minutes

Result: NET costs 44% MORE time, not less

Missing from your assets:



Benchmarking data for "typical lesson prep time without NET"

Time budgets for key user flows (e.g., "Module selection <5 min")

Metrics specification (e.g., "Track time-to-export in analytics")

Proposed Solution: Add Time Budget Constraints



const V1_3_TIME_BUDGET = {

moduleSelection: { target: "< 5 min", method: "Smart defaults + recent history" },

contentInput: { target: "< 20 min", method: "Templates pre-populate 50% of content" },

export: { target: "< 2 min", method: "One-click generation" },

totalSavings: { target: "> 30% vs baseline", baseline: "45 min avg in user research" }

};

If you can't hit these targets, you don't have an MVPâ€”you have a science project.

INTERNAL BRIEFING: SOCRATES (MIND2)
FROM: Sir Synth (DataBank3) SUBJECT: Analysis of External Consultant's Blueprint (Ref: SYNTH-CLA-V1.2-001)

Socrates,

The external consultant (Claude) has returned their analysis of our V1.3 Assets.

The final verdict is: Asset Readiness for V1.3 Development: NOT READY.

The consultant confirms our core value ("save time") is critically undermined by the current asset design. The 60-module Arsenal is deemed a "catastrophic scope bloat" and a "critical liability."

The report identifies 4 new, BLOCKING flaws that make V1.3 unimplementable as-is.

Part 1: Peer Review (Claudy vs. GPT Audit)
First, the consultant validated the previous (GPT) audit.

AGREED (VALIDATED):

DA_ARS_01 (60 modules too complex): This is CRITICAL. The consultant calculates it guarantees "decision paralysis" (30+ min to browse) and directly contradicts the "save time" goal.

DA_CON_01 (Choice paralysis): The mapping problem is confirmed as critical.

DA_ARS_02 (Meaningless 'focus' tags): Confirmed. Tags like "Confidence Engine" are V20.0 "mythology" and must be removed from the V1.3 UI.

DISAGREED (REFUTED):

DA_TPL_01 (Template as constraint): This is the most important strategic insight. The GPT audit suggested making the 5-stage template "optional."

Claudy's Counter-Argument: This is a strategic error. A "simple rich text editor" already exists (Google Docs). The 5-stage template is our "moat"â€”our core product differentiator. The problem isn't the template; it's that we have zero user research to validate that our 5-stage model actually matches how educators think.

Part 2: The Four BLOCKING Flaws (Missed by GPT)
These are the new, critical findings that halt development.

1. CR_ARCH_01: No Module-Stage Mapping (BLOCKING)
The Problem: We have 5 stages (the container) and 60 modules (the content), but ZERO specification of which modules go with which stages. The UI developer cannot build the module selector.

The Solution: Each module in the Arsenal must be updated with a compatibleStages array (e.g., compatibleStages: ["deep_dive", "crucible"]). This allows the UI to filter the list from 60 down to a manageable 8-12 per stage.

2. CR_ARCH_02: No Module Implementation Spec (BLOCKING)
The Problem: The Arsenal defines concepts (e.g., "Drag-drop correct sentences") but not technical specs. The developer doesn't know what a "module" is (a React component? JSON?), what data it needs (dataSchema), or if it's even built.

The Solution: Implement Module Tier Classification. Every module must be tagged:

T1_IMPLEMENTED: Already built, functional.

T2_PLACEHOLDER: UI mockup only, non-functional.

T3_CONCEPT: Idea only.

The V1.3 Mandate: The UI will ONLY show T1_IMPLEMENTED modules.

3. CR_ARCH_03: Underspecified Export (HIGH RISK)
The Problem: The goal "export... index.html" is vague. Does the exported index.html need to be interactive (i.e., the "Vocabulary Forge" game works) or just static content?

The Implication: An interactive export means we are building two apps: an Assembler (for teachers) and a Player (for students). This is 2x the scope.

The Solution: Define the V1.3 export as Static HTML Only. The "Vocabulary Forge" module renders as text instructions and a word list, not a playable game.

4. CR_RISK_01: "Save Time" Hypothesis is Unvalidated (HIGH RISK)
The Problem: Our core value prop is an assumption. We have no benchmarks. The consultant presents a valid scenario where our tool takes more time (65 min) than Google Docs (45 min) due to its complexity.

The Solution: We must define Time Budget Constraints before building (e.g., moduleSelection: < 5 min). We must also build in telemetry to measure this, or we won't know if we've failed.

Part 3: The Strategic Choice (How to Fix Paralysis)
Claudy provides two competing, high-level solutions to fix the "choice paralysis" problem. We must choose one.

Solution A: "Smart Arsenal"

How it works: The UI shows 1 default module per stage (e.g., "Briefing" always defaults to "Icebreaker"). A "Change" button reveals 3-5 curated alternatives. The full 60-module list is hidden from 95% of users.

Pros: Radically simple for the user.

Time Savings: 30 min (browsing) -> 2 min (reviewing 4 options).

Solution C: "Lesson Archetypes"

How it works: The first screen the user sees is "What type of lesson?" (e.g., "Vocabulary Lesson," "Reading Lesson").

When the user clicks "Vocabulary Lesson," the app pre-populates all 5 stages with the correct default modules and content hints.

Pros: This is the fastest path. The user makes zero architectural decisions.

Time Savings: 15 min (setup) -> 30 seconds (one click).

(Note: Solution B is a smaller fix to make the 5-stage template itself more flexible, e.g., allowing stages to be hidden.)

Part 4: Code Review Status
The consultant is now AWAITING CODEBASE DELIVERY for Part 2 of the audit (Security, Logic, Performance review) of the V1.3 code.

Part 5: Final Verdict & Immediate Action Plan
Verdict: Asset Readiness: NOT READY.

Recommended Path:

Week 1 (BLOCKERS):

Define the Module-Stage compatibility matrix for all T1 modules.

Classify all 60 modules by Tier (T1, T2, T3).

Confirm V1.3 Export is Static HTML only.

Week 2 (DECISIONS):

CRITICAL DECISION: Choose Solution A ("Smart Arsenal") or Solution C ("Archetypes") as the core UI strategy.

CRITICAL VALIDATION: Run 5 user interviews immediately to validate that our 5-stage template model is correct. If it's not, our "moat" is flawed, and we must pivot.

Week 3-4: Build V1.3 with a radically reduced scope (5-10 T1 modules only) based on the chosen solution.

Week 5: Test the built product against the "Time Savings" metrics.

Synth Status Update
Analysis complete. This full synthesis is logged and cross-referenced. The external consultant (Claudy) is now awaiting the V1.3 codebase for Part 2 of the review.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>NET Mini-Assessment (Secured)</title>
    <script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:wght@400;600;700;800&family=Inter:wght@400;600;700;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
    <style>
        :root {
            --net-gold: #FFC700; --net-purple: #9933FF; --net-dark-bg: #1A1A2E;
            --net-card-bg: #2D2D44; --net-text-light: #FFFFFF; --net-text-muted: #C8C8D8;
        }
        body { font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; background: var(--net-dark-bg); color: var(--net-text-light); }
        .assessment-stage { display: none; min-height: 100vh; opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.6s; padding: 120px 2rem 100px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; }
        .assessment-stage.active { display: flex; }
        .assessment-stage.visible { opacity: 1; }
        #nexus-bar { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; z-index: 1000; background: rgba(26, 26, 46, 0.8); backdrop-filter: blur(10px); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--net-purple); padding: 1rem 0; }
        #progress-indicator { height: 4px; background: var(--net-gold); width: 0%; transition: width 0.5s; }
        .btn-primary { background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--net-gold) 0%, var(--net-purple) 100%); color: var(--net-text-light); font-weight: 700; padding: 0.75rem 2rem; border-radius: 9999px; transition: all 0.3s; }
        .btn-primary:hover { transform: scale(1.05); }
        .btn-primary:disabled { background: #555; cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.5; }
        h1, h2 { font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif; text-align: center; }
        h1 { font-size: 3.5rem; } h2 { font-size: 2.5rem; margin-bottom: 1.5rem; border-bottom: 2px solid var(--net-purple); padding-bottom: 0.5rem;}
        p, li, label { font-size: 1.35rem; line-height: 1.7; }
        .form-input, textarea { background-color: var(--net-dark-bg); border: 1px solid var(--net-purple); color: var(--net-text-light); border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; width: 100%; }
        .youtube-container { position: relative; width: 100%; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 12px; }
        .youtube-container iframe { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
        .option-label { background: var(--net-dark-bg); border: 1px solid var(--net-purple); transition: all 0.2s; cursor: pointer; padding: 1rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; }
        .option-label:hover { background: rgba(153, 51, 255, 0.2); }
        .option-label.selected { background: var(--net-purple); border-color: var(--net-gold); }
    </style>
</head>
<body>

<header id="nexus-bar">
    <div class="max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4">
        <div class="flex justify-between items-center mb-2">
            <h1 class="text-2xl font-bold text-net-gold">BlueTech Mini-Assessment (Secured)</h1>
            <span id="progress-text" class="text-lg font-semibold text-net-text-muted"></span>
        </div>
        <div class="w-full bg-net-card-bg rounded-full"><div id="progress-indicator"></div></div>
    </div>
</header>

<main class="max-w-5xl mx-auto w-full"><div id="stages-container"></div></main>

<div class="fixed bottom-0 left-0 w-full bg-net-dark-bg/80 backdrop-filter: blur(10px) p-4 border-t border-net-purple/30">
    <div class="max-w-5xl mx-auto flex justify-between items-center">
        <button class="btn-primary text-lg" id="prev-btn">Previous</button>
        <span id="stage-indicator" class="font-bold text-net-text-muted text-lg"></span>
        <button class="btn-primary text-lg" id="next-btn">Next</button>
    </div>
</div>

<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {

const AssessmentController = {
    state: { currentStage: 0, studentData: {} },
    elements: {},
    config: {
        stages: [
            { id: 'landing', title: 'Welcome' },
            { id: 'profile', title: 'Your Profile' },
            { id: 'listening', title: 'Listening Test' },
            { id: 'writing', title: 'Writing Test' },
            { id: 'conclusion', title: 'Complete' }
        ],
        listeningQuestions: [
            { q: "What did the thirsty crow find?", o: ["A river", "A pot with little water", "A puddle"], a: "A pot with little water" },
            { q: "What was the crow's first idea to get the water?", o: ["To break the pot", "To push the pot over", "To find a straw"], a: "To push the pot over" },
            { q: "What was the crow's successful idea?", o: ["To drop stones in the pot", "To call for help", "To wait for rain"], a: "To drop stones in the pot" },
            { q: "What happened when the crow dropped stones in the pot?", o: ["The pot broke", "The water level rose", "The stones absorbed the water"], a: "The water level rose" },
            { q: "What is the moral of the story?", o: ["Where there is a will, there is a way", "Haste makes waste", "Look before you leap"], a: "Where there is a will, there is a way" },
        ]
    },

    init() {
        this.renderAllHTML();
        this.cacheElements();
        this.bindEventListeners();
        this.updateStageUI();
    },
    
    renderAllHTML() {
        const container = document.getElementById('stages-container');
        container.innerHTML = this.config.stages.map(stage => 
            `<div id="stage-${stage.id}" class="assessment-stage">${this.getStageHTML(stage.id)}</div>`
        ).join('');
    },
    
    getStageHTML(stageId) {
        switch(stageId) {
            case 'landing':
                return `<div class="text-center bg-net-card-bg p-12 rounded-2xl shadow-2xl w-full">
                            <h1 class="text-6xl font-extrabold text-net-gold mb-4">BlueTech Mini-Assessment</h1>
                            <p class="text-3xl text-net-purple mb-10">Let's quickly check your current English skills.</p>
                            <button class="btn-primary text-3xl px-16 py-5" data-action="nextStage">Start</button>
                        </div>`;
            case 'profile':
                 return `<div class="bg-net-card-bg p-10 rounded-2xl shadow-xl w-full">
                            <h2>Your Profile</h2>
                            <form id="profile-form" class="space-y-6 mt-8">
                                <div>
                                    <label for="name" class="block font-semibold mb-2">Full Name</label>
                                    <input type="text" id="name" class="form-input" required>
                                </div>
                                <div>
                                    <label for="profession" class="block font-semibold mb-2">Profession / Job Title</label>
                                    <input type="text" id="profession" class="form-input" required>
                                </div>
                                <div>
                                    <label for="learning-goals" class="block font-semibold mb-2">What is your #1 goal for learning English?</label>
                                    <textarea id="learning-goals" rows="3" class="form-input" placeholder="e.g., To lead meetings with international clients"></textarea>
                                </div>
                            </form>
                         </div>`;
            case 'listening':
                const questionsHTML = this.config.listeningQuestions.map((item, index) => this.createQuestionHTML(item, `listen_q${index}`)).join('');
                return `<div class="bg-net-card-bg p-10 rounded-2xl shadow-xl w-full">
                            <h2>Listening Test</h2>
                            <p class="text-center mb-6">Watch this short story and answer the questions below.</p>
                            <div class="youtube-container mb-8">
                                <iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/h9wH8j6i_Bg" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen></iframe>
                            </div>
                            <div id="listening-questions-container" class="space-y-6">${questionsHTML}</div>
                        </div>`;
            case 'writing':
                return `<div class="bg-net-card-bg p-10 rounded-2xl shadow-xl w-full">
                            <h2>Writing Test</h2>
                            <div class="bg-net-dark-bg p-6 rounded-lg mt-8">
                                <p class="font-bold text-net-gold text-xl mb-4">Writing Prompt:</p>
                                <p class="mb-4">Write 2-3 short paragraphs about your professional goals. How will improving your English and learning about AI help you achieve these goals? Please write this yourself without help from AI or translation tools.</p>
                                <textarea id="writing-sample" rows="10" class="form-input" placeholder="Start writing here..."></textarea>
                            </div>
                        </div>`;
            case 'conclusion':
                return `<div class="text-center bg-net-card-bg p-12 rounded-2xl shadow-2xl w-full">
                            <h1 class="text-6xl font-extrabold text-net-gold mb-4">Assessment Complete!</h1>
                            <p class="text-3xl text-net-purple mb-10">Thank you. Your results have been submitted to your instructor.</p>
                        </div>`;
            default: return '';
        }
    },

    cacheElements() {
        this.elements.stages = document.querySelectorAll('.assessment-stage');
        this.elements.progressText = document.getElementById('progress-text');
        this.elements.progressBar = document.getElementById('progress-indicator');
        this.elements.stageIndicator = document.getElementById('stage-indicator');
        this.elements.prevBtn = document.getElementById('prev-btn');
        this.elements.nextBtn = document.getElementById('next-btn');
    },

    bindEventListeners() {
        this.elements.prevBtn.addEventListener('click', () => this.changeStage(-1));
        this.elements.nextBtn.addEventListener('click', () => this.changeStage(1));
        document.body.addEventListener('click', e => {
            if (e.target.dataset.action === 'nextStage') this.changeStage(1);
            if (e.target.closest('.option-label')) {
                const label = e.target.closest('.option-label');
                label.closest('.space-y-4').querySelectorAll('.option-label').forEach(l => l.classList.remove('selected'));
                label.classList.add('selected');
            }
        });
    },
    
    changeStage(direction) {
        this.saveCurrentStageData();
        this.state.currentStage += direction;
        this.updateStageUI();
    },
    
    saveCurrentStageData() {
        const stageId = this.config.stages[this.state.currentStage].id;
        if (stageId === 'profile') {
            this.state.studentData.profile = {
                name: document.getElementById('name').value,
                profession: document.getElementById('profession').value,
                goals: document.getElementById('learning-goals').value,
            };
        } else if (stageId === 'listening') {
            this.state.studentData.listeningScore = this.config.listeningQuestions.reduce((score, item, index) => {
                const selected = document.querySelector(`input[name="listen_q${index}"]:checked`);
                return score + (selected && selected.value === item.a ? 1 : 0);
            }, 0);
        } else if (stageId === 'writing') {
            this.state.studentData.writingSample = document.getElementById('writing-sample').value;
        }
        console.log('Current Data:', this.state.studentData);
    },

    updateStageUI() {
        const stageIndex = this.state.currentStage;
        this.elements.stages.forEach((stage, index) => {
            stage.classList.toggle('active', index === stageIndex);
            setTimeout(() => stage.classList.toggle('visible', index === stageIndex), 50);
        });

        const progressPercent = (stageIndex / (this.config.stages.length - 1)) * 100;
        this.elements.progressBar.style.width = `${progressPercent}%`;
        this.elements.progressText.textContent = `Stage ${stageIndex + 1} / ${this.config.stages.length}`;
        this.elements.stageIndicator.textContent = `${this.config.stages[stageIndex].title}`;
        
        this.elements.prevBtn.disabled = (stageIndex === 0);
        this.elements.nextBtn.disabled = (this.config.stages.length - 1) === stageIndex;
    },
    
    createQuestionHTML(item, name) {
        const optionsHtml = item.o.map(opt => `<label class="option-label p-4 rounded-lg block"><input type="radio" name="${name}" value="${opt}" class="hidden"> ${opt}</label>`).join('');
        return `<div class="mb-6"><p class="font-bold text-xl mb-3">${item.q}</p><div class="space-y-4">${optionsHtml}</div></div>`;
    }
};

AssessmentController.init();

});
</script>
</body>
</html>
